initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The current board has only two pieces placed at the bottom row: 'o' in column 2 and 'x' in column 3. All columns remain playable since the top row is empty. As player 'x', the goal is to select a move that controls the most valuable space on the board while setting up multiple lines for a future 4-in-a-row.

The center column (index 3) is the single most important column in Connect 4 because it participates in the largest number of potential winning combinations: one vertical line, two diagonal lines (both directions), and a central horizontal line. Placing in column 3 stacks a second 'x' directly on top of the existing piece, creating an early vertical pair in the center. This is a strong foundational move that keeps options open for expansion upward or horizontally from that column.

Alternative moves are inferior:
- Column 4 creates a horizontal pair at the bottom but shifts focus away from the true center.
- Column 2 places on top of the opponent's piece, which is inefficient and gives the opponent easy counterplay around it.
- Columns 0, 1, 5, and 6 are too far from the center and create fewer overlapping threats.

No immediate win or forced threat exists after any single move, so the long-term positional advantage of the center column makes index 3 optimal.

Final Answer: 3

The only moves that immediately connect to these pieces are column 2 (creating an L-shape at rows 4-5) or column 4 (creating a mirrored L-shape at rows 4-5). Column 3 is suboptimal because it places an x above the o at row 3, isolating the new piece from the existing stack. All other columns (0, 1, 5, 6) leave the new x disconnected from the existing pieces.

A one-move lookahead shows column 4 is superior. Placing an x at row 5, column 4 creates a connected L (horizontal at row 5, columns 3-4; vertical at column 3, rows 4-5; diagonal between row 4/column 3 and row 5/column 4). Regardless of o's response:
- If o plays anywhere except column 4, the follow-up move in column 5 creates three-in-a-row horizontally at row 5 (columns 3-5), forcing o to block at column 6.
- If o plays in column 4 (at row 4), the follow-up in column 4 creates a strong 2x2 square, setting up multiple future threats (horizontal extensions at rows 4 and 5).

In contrast, starting in column 2 allows o a safe response (e.g., stacking in column 3 at row 2 to build vertically), after which no immediate three-in-a-row is available and the position becomes a less-forcing staircase. Column 4 therefore creates forcing pressure faster while maintaining flexibility for future forks.

Final Answer: 4
